answer: Practically, the chain should mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because opal only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, anchor is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any harbor approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
